S024.name: Depressed_Mood
S024.description: A state where a sad, empty, or hopeless mood persists.

subtypes.Depressed Mood: A persistently sunken mood or feeling of depression.
subtypes.Tearfulness: A state of frequent crying or inability to hold back tears.
subtypes.Sadness: A state where a sad or gloomy mood is maintained continuously.
subtypes.Emptiness: A feeling of inner emptiness or a state of feeling no emotion.
subtypes.Emotional Numbness: A state where emotions feel dulled or paralyzed.

S025.name: Loss_of_Interest
S025.description: A state where interest or pleasure in previously enjoyed activities is markedly diminished.

subtypes.Loss of Interest: Reduced interest in previously enjoyed hobbies or leisure activities.
subtypes.Social Withdrawal: Reduced interest or effort in social interactions and maintaining relationships.
subtypes.Loss of Motivation: Lack of motivation to initiate or complete work or tasks.
subtypes.Anhedonia: Inability to experience positive emotions such as happiness, satisfaction, love, or pleasure.
subtypes.Indifference to Achievement: Insensitivity or indifference to personal achievements or success.

S026.name: Weight_Appetite_Change
S026.description: Significant increase or decrease in appetite or weight.

subtypes.Significant Weight Loss: Weight loss of more than 5% in a month without dieting.
subtypes.Weight Gain: Weight gain of more than 5% in a month.
subtypes.Decrease in Appetite: Decrease in appetite occurring nearly every day.
subtypes.Increase in Appetite: Increase in appetite occurring nearly every day.

S027.name: Sleep_Disturbance
S027.description: A state where there is a significant change in the quantity or quality of sleep.

subtypes.Initial Insomnia: Difficulty falling asleep and taking a long time to do so.
subtypes.Middle Insomnia: Waking up frequently during sleep or having difficulty falling back asleep.
subtypes.Early Morning Awakening: Waking up too early and being unable to fall back asleep.
subtypes.Hypersomnia: Sleeping for long periods at night or excessive sleep during the day.
subtypes.Nightmare Disorder: Sleep disturbance caused by repeated and distressing dreams.
subtypes.Non-Restorative Sleep: Feeling unrefreshed despite having slept enough.

S028.name: Psychomotor_Changes
S028.description: Observable increase or decrease in psychomotor activity.

subtypes.Psychomotor Agitation: Purposeless repetitive behaviors such as inability to sit still, pacing, hand-wringing, or picking at skin.
subtypes.Psychomotor Retardation (Motor): Visible slowing of general body movements, such as walking speed or picking up objects.
subtypes.Psychomotor Retardation (Speech): Long response latency or slowed speech when asked a question.

S029.name: Fatigue
S029.description: Persistent fatigue that is not relieved by rest and a marked lack of energy.

subtypes.Chronic Fatigue: Fatigue that persists for a long period even after adequate rest.
subtypes.Physical Fatigue: A state of physical exhaustion where the body feels heavy and easily tires even from minor activities.
subtypes.Mental Fatigue: A state where fatigue accumulates rapidly during the process of thinking or concentrating.
subtypes.Loss of Energy: Difficulty performing daily activities due to a decline in energy and vitality.

S030.name: Worthlessness_Guilt
S030.description: Feelings of worthlessness or excessive or inappropriate guilt (which may be delusional; not merely self-reproach or guilt about being sick).

subtypes.Feelings of Worthlessness: The feeling that one is useless and has no value.
subtypes.Ruminative Guilt: A thought pattern of obsessively replaying past minor mistakes or flaws and constantly reproaching oneself.
subtypes.Excessive or Inappropriate Guilt: Feeling excessive responsibility for trivial matters or daily events and believing one deserves punishment.
subtypes.Delusional Guilt: Guilt reaching a delusional level, disconnected from reality, involving feeling responsible for unrelated unfortunate events.

S031.name: Diminished_Thinking
S031.description: Diminished ability to think or concentrate, or indecisiveness.

subtypes.Reduced Concentration: Unable to pay attention or maintain focus on specific activities like conversation, reading, or watching TV.
subtypes.Indecisiveness: Extreme difficulty making even minor daily choices (e.g., menu, clothes) and hesitating to make decisions.
subtypes.Subjective Memory Complaints: Complaining of memory decline, such as forgetting where things were placed, due to reduced focus.
subtypes.Clouded Thinking: Thinking feels foggy, dazed, or not clear.

S033.name: Elevated_Irritable_Mood
S033.description: A distinct period of abnormally and persistently elevated, expansive, or irritable mood.

subtypes.Elevated Mood: A mood that is abnormally high, euphoric, and full of unmotivated happiness and vitality.
subtypes.Irritable Mood: A state where one gets angry or aggressive even at minor stimuli.
subtypes.Mood Lability: Rapid shifts in mood, alternating unpredictably between euphoria and irritability.

S034.name: Increased_Activity
S034.description: Abnormally and persistently increased goal-directed activity or energy.

subtypes.Increased Energy: Overflowing physical and mental energy, leading to an inability to stay still and a desire to keep moving.
subtypes.Hyperactivity: Doing far more work than usual or starting multiple activities simultaneously.
subtypes.Psychomotor Agitation: Inability to tolerate resting or stopping, driven by a constant need to do something.

S035.name: Inflated_Self_Esteem
S035.description: Inflated self-esteem or grandiosity (may range from uncritical self-confidence to delusional proportions).

subtypes.Inflated Self-Confidence: Feeling capable of anything and believing that failure is impossible, unlike one's usual self.
subtypes.Overestimation of Abilities: Unrealistically assessing one's talents, knowledge, or abilities as superior.
subtypes.Grandiose Delusions: The false belief that one is a special and important person with a special mission or purpose.

S036.name: Decreased_Sleep
S036.description: Decreased need for sleep (e.g., feels rested after only 3 hours of sleep).

subtypes.Reduced Sleep Duration: Sleeping significantly less than usual but feeling refreshed rather than tired.
subtypes.Loss of Sleep Need: Not feeling the urge to sleep or the thought that sleep is necessary.
subtypes.Indifference to Insomnia: Feeling no problem and continuing activities despite staying up for several nights.

S037.name: Pressured_Speech
S037.description: More talkative than usual or pressure to keep talking.

subtypes.Talkativeness: Speaking far more than usual and continuing to talk without rest.
subtypes.Rapid Speech: Speech speed is so fast that it is difficult for others to understand or interrupt.
subtypes.Pressured Speech: Cannot stop talking or tolerate silence due to an internal pressure to keep speaking.

S038.name: Racing_Thoughts
S038.description: Flight of ideas or subjective experience that thoughts are racing.

subtypes.Racing Thoughts: Thoughts spinning too fast in the head, constantly jumping from one idea to another.
subtypes.Flooding of Thoughts: Too many thoughts emerging simultaneously, making them disorganized.
subtypes.Inability to Control Thoughts: Unable to stop or slow down thoughts and unable to calm the mind.

S040.name: Increased_Goal_Activity
S040.description: Increase in goal-directed activity (at work, school, socially, or sexually) or purposeless psychomotor agitation.

subtypes.Occupational Hyperactivity: Driving significantly more projects or work than usual in the workplace or academic setting.
subtypes.Social Hyperactivity: Becoming much more sociable and extroverted than usual, actively meeting and contacting people.
subtypes.Hypersexuality: Significantly increased interest in or activity regarding sex.
subtypes.Psychomotor Agitation: Purposeless non-goal-directed activity, such as pacing or hand-wringing, driven by an inability to sit still.

symptom.disease_info: Bipolar II Disorder is characterized by a recurrent course of depressive episodes and hypomanic episodes, with no history of full manic episodes. Hypomanic periods involve persistently elevated, expansive, or irritable mood and increased energy, but without the marked impairment, hospitalization, or psychosis seen in mania. Depressive episodes are often more frequent and disabling, and patients typically present during these lows rather than during hypomania, which may be experienced as productive or ego-syntonic. It is distinguished from unipolar depression by the presence of hypomanic episodes and from Bipolar I Disorder by the absence of full mania, and it commonly emerges in late adolescence or early adulthood with a chronic, episodic course.

patient.stressor: For Marta, the turning point came during a particularly tense season at home and work, when her teenage daughter was pushing against family rules and her spouse was working longer hours, leaving her feeling caught in the middle. Around the same time, a successful rollout of a new hospitality program at her workplace left her unusually energized and socially outgoing for several weeks, leading her to impulsively add new initiatives and overcommit to community events and art workshops. As that surge of activity tapered off, she found herself increasingly emotionally raw and self‑critical about minor conflicts with staff and family, canceling hikes and yoga classes and having trouble keeping up with schedules she used to manage despite her relaxed style. After a heated argument with her daughter about her inconsistency at home and a colleague gently suggesting she seemed "not like herself" for the past month, Marta consulted her primary care provider, who referred her for psychiatric assessment to understand the pattern behind these fluctuating periods and the strain they were placing on her relationships.
patient.chief_complaint: “Lately I’ve been overwhelmed by guilt about letting everyone down at home and at work, even when people tell me it’s not that bad.”

S024.name: Depressed_Mood
S024.description: A state where a sad, empty, or hopeless mood persists.
S024.manifestation: Most days lately I wake up with this heavy, gray feeling in my chest, like something inside me has sunk, and even small things—like my daughter rolling her eyes or an email from my boss—can make me feel on the verge of tears for no clear reason.

S025.name: Loss_of_Interest
S025.description: A state where interest or pleasure in previously enjoyed activities is markedly diminished.
S025.manifestation: I used to really look forward to my Saturday hikes and my art class, but over the past few weeks I keep canceling because I just can’t seem to care enough to get out the door, and even when I force myself to go it all feels flat and pointless.

S026.name: Weight_Appetite_Change
S026.description: Significant increase or decrease in appetite or weight.
S026.manifestation: I’ve noticed that most days I either pick at my food or skip meals without really meaning to, and when I finally weigh myself I see I’ve dropped a few pounds because I just don’t feel hungry or interested in eating.

S027.name: Sleep_Disturbance
S027.description: A state where there is a significant change in the quantity or quality of sleep.
S027.manifestation: At night I lie in bed for what feels like hours, my mind replaying arguments from home and little mistakes at work, and even when I finally fall asleep I wake up a couple of times and never feel rested in the morning.

S028.name: Psychomotor_Changes
S028.description: Observable increase or decrease in psychomotor activity.
S028.manifestation: Lately my body feels like it’s moving through molasses—people at work have commented that I walk slower down the hallway and I catch myself just staring at the computer before I can make my fingers start typing an email.

S029.name: Fatigue
S029.description: Persistent fatigue that is not relieved by rest and a marked lack of energy.
S029.manifestation: No matter how much I try to rest, I feel exhausted all day, to the point that just getting ready for work or loading the dishwasher feels like it takes everything I’ve got.

S030.name: Worthlessness_Guilt
S030.description: Feelings of worthlessness or excessive or inappropriate guilt (which may be delusional; not merely self-reproach or guilt about being sick).
S030.manifestation: I keep going over every little thing I’ve said or done, like snapping at my daughter or missing a deadline, and I end up convinced I’m a terrible mother and a lousy manager who’s letting everyone down, even when people tell me I’m being too hard on myself.

S031.name: Diminished_Thinking
S031.description: Diminished ability to think or concentrate, or indecisiveness.
S031.manifestation: In meetings and even at home when my husband is talking, my mind just sort of blanks out and I lose the thread of what’s being said, and simple decisions like what to cook for dinner can leave me standing in the kitchen frozen for ten minutes.

S033.name: Elevated_Irritable_Mood
S033.description: A distinct period of abnormally and persistently elevated, expansive, or irritable mood.
S033.manifestation: Right before this slump, there was a stretch where I felt unusually upbeat and almost touchy at the same time—one moment I was joking and buzzing with ideas about new programs, and the next I’d snap at my daughter over something minor and then wonder why I’d overreacted.

S034.name: Increased_Activity
S034.description: Abnormally and persistently increased goal-directed activity or energy.
S034.manifestation: During that energized period after the program launch, I couldn’t sit still at work—I was starting new projects, volunteering for extra committees, and signing up for community art events all at once, as if I had to keep doing more and more.

S035.name: Inflated_Self_Esteem
S035.description: Inflated self-esteem or grandiosity (may range from uncritical self-confidence to delusional proportions).
S035.manifestation: For a few weeks after the rollout, I caught myself thinking, “I’m really the only one here who knows how to turn this place around,” and I felt oddly certain that I could handle anything without needing much help from anyone.

S036.name: Decreased_Sleep
S036.description: Decreased need for sleep (e.g., feels rested after only 3 hours of sleep).
S036.manifestation: In that same high-energy phase, I was going to bed well after midnight, getting maybe four hours of sleep, and still waking up wired and ready to dive into emails or planning another project without feeling tired at all.

S037.name: Pressured_Speech
S037.description: More talkative than usual or pressure to keep talking.
S037.manifestation: My coworkers even joked that I wouldn’t let anyone get a word in, because in meetings I’d talk fast and jump from one idea to the next without pausing long enough for people to respond.

S038.name: Racing_Thoughts
S038.description: Flight of ideas or subjective experience that thoughts are racing.
S038.manifestation: Especially during those weeks when I was riding that high, my thoughts felt like they were racing ahead of me—while I was explaining one idea, my brain was already three ideas ahead, and it was hard to slow myself down.

S040.name: Increased_Goal_Activity
S040.description: Increase in goal-directed activity (at work, school, socially, or sexually) or purposeless psychomotor agitation.
S040.manifestation: I went from my usual steady pace to suddenly filling my calendar with extra work projects, organizing a neighborhood art night, and trying to be at every school event, almost as if I needed to prove I could be everywhere and do everything at once.

add_requirements.functional_impairment: Over the past several months, I’ve started missing deadlines, forgetting meetings, and backing out of plans with friends and family, to the point that my team has had to quietly pick up my slack and my daughter has told me she doesn’t know which version of me she’s coming home to.
add_requirements.duration: Looking back, these cycles of feeling overly revved up for a few weeks and then sinking into long stretches of feeling low and drained have been happening on and off for at least a few years, but they’ve become especially noticeable since the pressures at home and work ramped up this past year.
add_requirements.depressive_episode_duration: This current low stretch has been dragging on for about five months now, starting not long after that busy high I had around the time of the program rollout at work.
